summary: Masaaki Tsuchiya works in sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kokugakuin University (~1980-1989) and held a post at Senshu University around 1996.

Masaharu Anesaki studied religious and Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo (~1893-1896), under Friedrich Max Müller (~1900), and at the University of Kiel under Paul Deussen (~1900-1902). He was a professor at the University of Tokyo (1904) and lectured at Collège de France (~1919-1920).

Masaharu Imai works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Tokyo University of Education (~1962-1970) and held posts at Ibaraki University (~1974-1990) and the University of Tsukuba (~1990-2006).

Masahide Mori specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Nagoya University (~1985-1987) and under Tadeusz Skorupski at the University of London/SOAS (1988-1997). His academic posts include Koyasan University (1994), Nagoya University (~1996-2000), and Kanazawa University (~2000-present).
Masahiro Asada is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1964-1974). He later served as an assistant professor at Ryukoku University (~1984-1991).
Masahiro Inami works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Hiroshima University (~1985-1990) and held positions at Tokyo Gakugei University from around 1996 to 2007 and beyond.

Masahiro Kusunoki specialized in religious and Buddhist studies, studying at Tohoku University (~1947-1953). He served as professor at Tohoku University (~1968-1985) and held leadership roles in the Tohoku Association of Indian and Religious Studies and the Japanese Association for Religious Studies.

Masahiro Shimoda is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (~1977-1994). He served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (~1991-2023) and held visiting appointments at SOAS, Stanford, and Virginia.
Masahiro Takano is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also served as a librarian (attested 1995).

Masakazu Tanaka is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Tohoku University (~1974-1980) and the London School of Economics and Political Science (~1981-1986). He held an academic post at Kyoto University from 1988 to 2019.

Masako Keta specializes in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Kyoto University (~1972-1980) and held posts at Aichi University of Technology Automotive Junior College (~1989-1994), Kanazawa University (~1994-2000), and Kyoto University (~2000-2019).

Masamichi Ichigo works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University, the University of Michigan, and Kyoto University under Susumu Yamaguchi, Yuichi Kajiyama, and Gadjin Nagao. He held faculty posts at Kyoto Sangyo University, Otani University, and Kyoto Koka Women's University.
Masamichi Sakai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna under supervisor Helmut Krasser (attested 2006, 2010).
Masanori Nakagawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer (attested 1991) and assistant professor of literature (attested 2002) at Chikushi Jogakuen University.

Masanori Shono specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He has held positions as an assistant professor at Osaka University (attested 2012) and as a researcher at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (attested 2015).

Masao Abe specialized in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Osaka City University and Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe, Shin'ichi Hisamatsu, Keiji Nishitani, and Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki. He held professorships at Nara University of Education, Kyoto University, and Pacific School of Religion.
Masao Shizutani specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history/archaeology. He held assistant professor posts at Josai University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (attested 1974).

Masao Yamaguchi worked in Japanology and religious studies, studying at the University of Tokyo (~1949-1953) and Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1955-1960). He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1967-1997), University of Shizuoka (~1997-1999), Sapporo University (~1999-2003), and Chuo University.

Masaru Akimoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He held appointments, including professor in the Faculty of Contemporary Social Studies, at Kyoto Women's University (attested 2002, 2015).
Masashi Nagai specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Komazawa University (~1965-1974) and later served there as an assistant professor (~1981-2017).
